But as with any divisional matchup in the NFL, there's always bound to be some unexpected surprises to unfold that make the events pan out a bit differently than the general consensus expects. That means Houston will have to rely on Anderson to carry a bit more of the load within the pass-rush than usual–– but considering he leads the lead in total sacks through 10 weeks, we know he's more than capable of doing just that. On top of Hunter's absence, though, the Colts will be dealing with some key injuries on their offensive line to starting tackles Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis. So Anderson––one of the best pass-rushers the NFL has to offer––will have the opportunity to go up against a pair of backup tackles on the Colts line coming off a short week. Last weekend against the Cleveland Browns, things got as bad as we've seen this season , as the Texans were called for a season-high 13 penalties and 112 yards. Impressively enough, four of those penalties were caused because of their special teams unit. Could the Texans magically turn a corner in this game and look like a more disciplined, refined unit to limit the penalties? It's always possible. Maybe the solution to those penalty problems finally clicked for DeMeco Ryans and this coaching staff after the events of last weekend. Despite that, the Colts have a win over Houston in 2026, and the Texans have struggled against just about everyone this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. After missing all of last season and the start of the 2026 season recovering from a brutal knee injury, Tank Dell is back – and thriving – with Stroud at quarterback. Dell and Stroud have some great chemistry in their time together in the NFL, and the young receiver has played just under 50 percent of the offensive snaps in back-to-back weeks. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. Dell isn’t going to lead this receiver room in snaps, but he’s getting looks from Stroud when he’s out there and is now facing a defense that is 18th in EPA/Pass, allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the league. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs withe ball during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Bullock · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:01 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, the other wants to win – but loses anyway. The baby horses currently lead the all-time series, 33-15-1 thanks in great part to the Peyton Manning/Marvin Harrison Sr. years. However, Houston has won 5 of past 6, thanks to the Colts no longer showing interest in winning football. On paper, as of this writing, the Texans should absolutely dominate this game – and very well may. H-Town QB C.J. Stroud is having an MVP season. The Houston wide receiver corps is one of the best in the league – including the son of the aforementioned Harrison Sr.. Their run game ran away when Joe Mixon suffered the mystery of the ages injury in 2024, but Stroud has still managed to find ways to complete 201 passes for 2462 yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 INTs. The offensive line remains offensive, mostly, but has had just enough get-in-the-way-ness to give Stroud time to throw. Currently, the Texans passing attack is 4th overall. Defensively, Houston has the horsepower to compete at an elite level, but due to off-coverage, injuries and what looks to be confusion with the gameplan, they're currently ranked 20th. Some believe it's a little too much "read your own press coverage", others blame coaching and play calling. In some ways it seems a desire to change up from last season to keep opponents guessing has taken this defense away from what they do best. If you're great at zigging, but decide to zag all the time cause you think your opponent is expecting the zig, then you need to be ok with ignoring your own strengths… We won't talk about the special teams… #ulcerinducing Meanwhile, over in the baby horse stable, the Colts are clearly trotting down the rebuild trail. So far in 2026 Indy has: A new owner who has taken direct control over the coaching staff An interim general manager (after firing their previous one late last month) Quenton Nelson: Traded to the Seattle Seahawks. DeForest Buckner: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs: Traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Keenan Allen: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. And managed to win 1 game since all these team-affecting moves. Their current goal seems to be the #1 draft pick, if the Los Angeles Chargers don't beat them to it. Colts vs Texans predictions: In true Houston Texans fashion, the Texans will beat an opponent who doesn't want to win. Just as they did to the aforementioned Chargers. The 2026 brand of Texans football doesn't defeat winning teams (exception: the Jacksonville Jaguars cause, #Glitter). They do, however, lose the battle to not win – meaning when an opponent wants to lose, they freely allow H-Town to go to town on them. Which will happen again tonight. Stroud will look like an MVP candidate on a national stage. The Colts will show all their dysfunction. And the talking heads will ignore the apparent incoming mutiny on Kirby Drive. Indianapolis Colts 13 Houston Texans 38 Those with a superficial knowledge of the Texans will beat the drum that they still have a shot at the playoffs, and how they've fixed their issues. Until the following week when they lose against the Baltimore Ravens at the end of the month. Meanwhile, those who do lift the hood and look beyond the check engine light glaring on this franchise's dashboard will see a different prediction: The end game pot is on the stove, simmering away. Chances are tonight will turn the burn down just long enough to have a nice Thanksgiving.

home.blurb: The Colts have ruled out five players ahead of Thursday night’s primetime Week 11 road game against the Texans , including three starters. Travis, missing his second straight game due to a knee injury, was banged up entering the Colts’ Week 9 home game but played. He missed all three of the team’s practices leading up to Week 10 and was ruled out prior to the game. Travis was estimated to have missed all three of the team’s practices -- had they been held this week -- as Colts head coach Shane Steichen opted for walkthrus. The Colts will also be without starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who left Sunday’s game with what was initially described as a shin injury. Ward has since been an estimated DNP throughout the team’s three walkthrus this week with a knee injury. Despite several injuries cropping up for Ward since the summer, this will be his first missed game of the year. Defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf) and tight end Will Mallory (hamstring) will both miss their second consecutive game for the Colts. The Colts have also listed four players, including starting cornerback Sauce Gardner , questionable. Gardner left Sunday’s game with an injury to the same left calf that held him out of Week 7 earlier this year and lost him four full games and parts of two more in the back-half of 2025. He was estimated to have missed all three practices this week. Starting long snapper Luke Rhodes , who missed just his second game in nearly a decade in Indianapolis, is also questionable with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 9 that cost him all three practices last week and ruled him out for Week 10. Rhodes was an estimated non-participant Monday but was limited Tuesday and Wednesday this week, a sign he’s moving in the right direction. Starting slot receiver and return man Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable, though he’s also trending in the right direction. Gould was limited in the team’s first two estimated practice reports this week, but he was listed as a full participant Wednesday. Offensive tackle Charlie Heck will not travel with the team to Houston on Wednesday due to personal reasons, and he’s also listed as questionable. away.headline: Miami Dolphins news roundup: Week 11 injury report includes Aaron Brewer update
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins will be without punter Bradley Pinoin on Sunday as they face the Buffalo Bills. Pinion has a right groin injury and missed practice all week before being ruled out on Friday's injury report. Miami signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad this week and is expected to elevate him to the active roster by today's 4 p.m. Eastern deadline. Miami also ruled out wide receiver Jared Wayne for Sunday's game. He has a quadriceps injury. The Dolphins injury report included cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee) and safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), both doubtful for the game. Cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee), center Aaron Brewer (concussion), and cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. (toe) are all questionable. Brewer, who missed last week's game with the head injury, fully participated in practice on Friday and, as long as he has no symptoms on Saturday, should be cleared to play. The Bills side of the reports includes cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) having been ruled out of the game while tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful. Safety Damar Hamlin (toe), defensive tackle T.J. Sanders (defensive tackle), and tight end Jackson Hawes (shoulder) are all questionable. You can check out more on the injury report news and other Dolphins news reports from around the web in this morning's edition of the Splash Zone: Dolphins' Hafley addresses who's in, who's out and who's in question for Sunday – Barry Jackson, Miami Herald The Dolphins have a good chance of getting back their starting center on Sunday at Buffalo, but they will likely be without one of their starting safeties. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

picks.blurb: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2). Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. Now it's their star pass-rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the season after celebrating a sack against the Patriots on Sunday. He joins a list that includes D.J. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. picks.blurb: Roundtable: Lions Week 11 Preview Against Buccaneers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 11 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. 1. How much is Aidan Hutchinson to blame for his ACL injury? Christian Booher: I think Hutchinson is definitely deserving of some blame for the fact that the injury occurred in such an unnecessary fashion. The movements that went into that injury have been analyzed, and it's rightfully pointed out that a move like the one he did to celebrate that sack poses a risk. However, it's such a fluke situation that it's hard to be extremely mad at the circumstances. He's done that celebration many times, and it just so happens that he has to learn of the risks this way. Vito Chirco: At the end of the day, it was a freak accident and could've happened to any one of the hundreds of players that celebrate after sacks and other big plays. However, as a defensive captain and veteran player now, he should've known better than to leave his feet to celebrate, especially after his previous season-ending injury just two years ago. Consequently, I believe it's fair to say that Hutchinson deserves to shoulder a fair portion of the blame for the ACL ailment. Emmett Matasovsky: It was not the smartest play by Aidan Hutchinson in that injury, I cannot lie. That said, the amount of negative comments towards the EDGE is a bit extreme this week. When a play like that happens, most players’ ligaments tend to be a few plays from giving during game action, frankly. It was not a smart celebration, especially with previous comments to stop the celebrations that could cause non-contact injuries. I will say it is a 60 percent Hutchinson fault, 40 percent circumstance of being close to a natural injury anyway. 2. Are Buccaneers going to be able to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs? Booher : I think the Lions will find some tough sledding on the ground throughout Sunday's game. The Buccaneers have had success against the Lions in past matchups when it comes to slowing down the run game, and with Vita Vea leading the charge, I think the Lions will once again struggle to run the ball. As a result, I think the key to victory is the right arm of Jared Goff, as he'll need to keep the offense on schedule through the air. Chirco : Despite the Buccaneers’ prowess against the run this season, I believe that Gibbs still ends up with a solid day on the ground. And you know that Drew Petzing will also deploy the dual-threat runner as often as possible as a receiver. I expect Gibbs to be contained a bit, but to still produce a couple of big runs in the Week 11 contest. Matasovsky : With the Buccaneers battered and the Lions with momentum, the best hope for Tampa Bay is that Gibbs has jetlag. I think it will be tough sledding for the Tampa defensive line. Gibbs has hit his stride and is coming off a performance of over 250 yards from scrimmage. The fatigue, especially post-international travel, might lead to more Vaki touches, but I do not see the Bucs stopping the Lions running backs room. 3. Who will be Detroit Lions game MVP? Booher : I think Goff is the MVP on Sunday. As I mentioned, the Lions could really struggle to run the ball, which puts more pressure on Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to dial up counters. Another player that I think is due for a big day is tight end Sam LaPorta, who will likely match up with former Detroit defensive standout Alex Anzalone throughout Sunday's game. Chirco : I'm going to go with Alim McNeill. The run-stuffing interior lineman has had an ultra productive campaign thus far this season, and he will need to come up big Sunday against Tampa Bay RB Bucky Irving. He also will be counted upon even more now as a pass-rusher due to the season-ending injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. With all this said, I believe he'll deliver a solid performance against the Buccaneers, keying a sixth straight victory for Detroit. Matasovsky : It would be foolish to not select Gibbs here. Jahmyr Gibbs has a chance to run free and make plays, especially if Yaya Diaby is out. The back will have a phenomenal backing up from his Munich game, with another effort over 100 yards rushing and two total touchdowns. 4. Will Kerby Joseph make a big impact this week? Booher : I'm tempering my expectations for Joseph in his first game of the season. More than anything, I want to see him be pain-free in his return to action. Before he was officially shut down last year, he would often depart games for a series at a time while dealing with this nagging knee injury, and so I want to see him get through the matchup without having to depart due to pain. Chirco : I'm going to say no. I think the All-Pro safety will log 45-50 total defensive snaps in his season debut. But ultimately, I believe he'll show signs of being hampered by his lingering knee issue. I'd temper my expectations from Joseph in this Week 11 matchup. Matasovsky : I can see this going both ways. I could see Kerby Joseph making a huge play, especially against potentially an undrafted rookie quarterback. However, I can also argue that I see Joseph on a “pitch count” and limited reps. Personally, I hope that it is the former, where Joseph announces he is back with an interception and gets his moment to celebrate in front of the home crowd. 5. What do you want to see from DE Ahmed Hassanein in his debut this season? Booher : Hassanein is a player that is easy to root for due to his mentality and his journey to the NFL. It's been a tough road since he was drafted by Detroit last year, but Sunday will be his first chance to prove he belongs. In the big end role that he will likely play, Hassanein needs to be firm in setting the edge, and I think he could also make an impact with a few pressures if he gets opportunities in passing downs. Chirco : I believe it's reasonable to expect Hassanein to garner a couple of QB hits and pressures in his NFL debut on Sunday. He faces a difficult task going up against the slippery Baker Mayfield. However, the Lions will be counting on the Boise State product to make life at least a little bit difficult for the veteran passer. Matasovsky : Hassanein will have a chance to make an impact, but I will settle for the Boise State product at least making a mark on the box score. It is tough to argue that he deserves more reps than a red hot Derrick Moore, who has four sacks in the last two outings. The former Lions sixth-round pick has earned the right to play, and was likely going to get a chance before Hutchinson’s injury prompted the move up the depth chart. That said, now is the time for the Egyptian. I want to see the player do his job and make positive plays, even if it is not a box score-stuffing day. At the end of the day, the second-year pro is a role player, and football is a game where all 11 players doing their job and role means a successful day. Simply put, I want a penalty free, “plus” day from Hassanein. Published Nov 22, 2026 VITO CHIRCO Vito has covered the NFL and the Detroit Lions for the past five years. Has extensive reporting history of college athletics, the Detroit Tigers and Detroit Mercy Athletics. Chirco's work include NFL columns, analyzing potential Detroit Lions prospects coming out of college, NFL draft coverage and analysis of events occurring in the NFL. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football 49ers rout Vikings Tarik Skubal to Mets Week 11 winners and losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners and losers 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 Andrew Hughes · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:23 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come out of their bye at 3-6, and they've lost six games by seven points or fewer . A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. home.headline: Lions HC Campbell Reacts to Jameson Williams' Front Flip Celebration After Aidan Hutchinson's Injury
home.blurb: Bleacher Report • 3h 49ers OT Likely Out for Season After Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack, head coach Dan Campbell is understandably wary of other in-game celebrations. So when star receiver Jameson Williams celebrated his 57-yard touchdown reception in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers by doing a front flip into the end zone, Campbell couldn't help but feel a rush of nerves. "He wants your heart to stop," Campbell jokingly told The Athletic's Michael Silver via text. Skattebo Explains Backflip Despite Plans to Stop Williams indicated that he doesn't intend to stop his touchdown celebrations, telling ESPN's Lindsey Thiry that he hopes to stick the landing the next time he scores. "I tried to land it. I didn't really know what to do, so I just did a front flip. I'm gonna try to land one later in the year for y'all, for sure," he said. Despite Campbell's internal struggle while watching Williams launch himself into the end zone, he didn't change his demeanor for his players. Silver noted that Campbell "was barely fazed, as is his custom." He also called the 50-year-old "a strong, steadying presence" for Detroit in the wake of devastating injuries to Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell (neck). ▶️ Full Bucs-Lions Recap 04:33 Even without two of their best defensive players, the Lions extended their streak of holding opponents to 275 or fewer total yards to four straight games. After improving to 8-2, Detroit has firmly established itself as one of the top contenders in the NFC. "That's been the biggest growth for us," Campbell said after the game , referring to the team's defensive consistency. "The improvement we've had in that group even after losing guys, that's the sign of a championship team." home.blurb: Mayfield said he practiced in a "limited fashion." The thumb injury held him out of action for three games. After Mayfield returned, he led the Buccaneers to two crucial divisional victories over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons — although the team didn't need him to complete a single pass in the latter contest. Bleacher Report • 3h 49ers OT Likely Out for Season Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is active for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported earlier Sunday morning that Mayfield "is determined to play through" the injury described as "a painful case of plantar fasciitis." Top Teams Make Their Super Bowl Case 🗣️ Mayfield suffered a foot sprain during Tampa Bay's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. He's still dealing with pain from the injury but was "pushing through it," according to NFL insider James Palmer . "He also has been dealing with the aftereffects of a dislocated right thumb suffered in Week 2 that sidelined him for three games. Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that. (Ayrton Breckenridge/USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co) Pete Grathoff · Kansas City Star Sat, November 21, 2026 at 6:43 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals franchise history dates to 1920 when the team began play in Chicago. This year's team has a chance to do something unseen in franchise history: Defeat the Chiefs in Kansas City. The Cardinals left Chicago for St. Louis in 1960, the same year the Chiefs began play in the American Football League. In 1988, the Cardinals moved to Arizona. No matter what city the Cardinals have called home, they have never won in Kansas City. The Chiefs hold a 5-0-1 record all-time against the Cardinals, and that tie sounds like it was a barn burner: 6-6 in 1970. The national NFL pundits don't think the Cardinals will get that first win in KC on Sunday. Here is how 67 national experts see things playing out in Sunday's game, which starts at noon and will be broadcast on KCTV (Ch. 5). A 27-13 Chiefs win is the outlook from the Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff, who wrote: "Carson Beck and the Cardinals were embarrassed in a 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10. More embarrassment is coming for Arizona. Kansas City will be too tough at home." A 27-12 Chiefs victory is the call from the Associated Press' Rob Maaddi. Here is an excerpt from his story: "The Cardinals upset the Rams in Los Angeles with Jacoby Brissett and they rallied to beat the Cowboys in Dallas with Gardner Minshew coming off the bench. Patrick Mahomes, with help from several rookies, had a big game in Atlanta." A 31-13 Chiefs win is the prediction from the Sporting News' Bill Bender. This is an excerpt from his story: "The Chiefs are favored by (a) huge spread. The Cardinals were awful in Carson Beck's debut, in which he had 105 passing yards, two interceptions and took five sacks." A 34-10 Chiefs win is the call from NBC Sports' Mike Florio. He wrote: "They're getting the Cardinals at the perfect time. Then again, pretty much any time anyone gets the Cardinals is the perfect time." The Chiefs will win 28-17 , says the Los Angeles Times' Sam Farmer. This is from his story: "Even without Kenneth Walker III, the Chiefs beat Atlanta with ease. The Cardinals hang tough, but they're playing a rookie quarterback making his second start. Winning in Kansas City is a tall order." They have moved on from wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. — once considered a generational draft prospect. Then, they saw their top wide receiver Michael Wilson lost for the season due to a neck injury. After trading away Week 1 starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, the Cardinals have entrusted the offense to rookie Carson Beck — although he is dealing with back spasms and may hand the reins to veteran Josh Johnson . FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as massive 15.5-point home favorites. After the Chiefs comfortably won their Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons , the Cardinals were on the wrong side of a 34-6 home blowout against the Los Angeles Rams . This will be Arizona's first regular season trip to Arrowhead Stadium since 2018 — when a quarterback named Patrick Mahomes made his 11th career start. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) The version of the Chiefs we saw in the second half both against the Falcons and the New York Jets the week before could hang 50 on Arizona if they wanted to. With a Thursday showdown with the Buffalo Bills looming, however, the bigger priority will be to shorten the game and minimize injury risk. I think the Chiefs will build a game plan around Emmett Johnson that prioritizes a moving clock. A low number of total possessions will keep this one from getting completely out of hand. Chiefs 24, Cardinals 9 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) On Sunday, the Chiefs need to come in and quickly take care of business against the Cardinals, with much larger games on the horizon. Despite the Cardinals' tight end Trey McBride being outstanding, the Chiefs defense should not have any issues handling the Cardinals' offense. I would look for Steve Spagnuolo to dial up the pressure early and often to try to force turnovers. The Chiefs are coming off a monster offensive showing against the Atlanta Falcons, but they could be down the entire right side of their offensive line with Trey Smith and Jaylon Moore both not practicing on Wednesday. Kenneth Walker will likely sit as well, giving Emmet Johnson the green light for another big day against the league's 28th-ranked run defense. Get in, get out, stay healthy. Chiefs 27, Cardinals 6 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs beating the Cardinals because I trust Mahomes and Andy Reid to find answers if the offense starts slow. And if Steve Spagnuolo gets Arizona into third-and-long and can turn Chris Jones loose, I don't see the Cardinals putting up enough points to keep up. Chiefs 38, Cardinals 13 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs should take care of business against Arizona, and with a Thanksgiving trip to Buffalo approaching, this is a game they need to control early. The Cardinals are tied for 31st in points allowed, while Kansas City has scored at least 30 in five of its seven wins. What I've liked about the Chiefs lately is that they've finished off struggling opponents instead of letting them hang around. I expect that to continue Sunday, with Steve Spagnuolo disguising coverages and creating problems for Arizona's offense with whoever is playing quarterback. I expect Kansas City to give Kenneth Walker III another week to recover, leaving Emmett Johnson with another opportunity to carry the load after his impressive first start. The ideal outcome is building a comfortable lead by the third quarter and giving the starters some rest before the short turnaround to Buffalo. The Chiefs still have to earn that opportunity, but this is a matchup they should control on both sides of the ball. I expect another convincing win. away.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

away.headline: Cardinals get bad news on Carson Beck’s status for Week 11 amid back injury
away.blurb: Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jeremiyah Love are all out for an extended period of time. Only Love might be back at some point this season. Carson Beck is throwing to a lackluster supporting cast. But now even he is banged up. Beck went on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, putting his status for Week 11 in doubt. That doubt now appears to be close to a certainty, as the expectation is Beck will be ruled out for the Chiefs game. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals have their starting quarterback battling through an injury heading into the Week 11 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Carson Beck popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant with a back injury. However, he seemed to be walking normally in the locker room after practice that was open to the media. This is not the first time this season that Beck is dealing with a back injury, having dealt with it earlier in the year. The Arizona Cardinals have handed the reigns of the franchise to rookie quarterback Carson Beck. After trading away starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the trade deadline, the former Georgia Bulldog has been the franchise’s next hope. While he is looking to improve as he gets more experience, he is dealing with an injury that made him pop up on the injury report. Let’s take a closer look at to what Carson Beck’s injury is and what it means for the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona Cardinals place Carson Beck on Thursday’s injury report Carson Beck struggled last week in his NFL debut against the Los Angeles Rams. He completed 11 of 18 (61.1%) of his passes for 108 yards with zero touchdowns and two interceptions while also being sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals are dealing with a lot of injuries on the offensive side of the ball, so protecting Carson Beck and moving the football could be a challenge. If Beck is unable to go for Week 11, Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar are the backups on the roster. However, neither quarterback has been with the Arizona Cardinals for more than two weeks. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center. It hasn’t been the season the Eagles have hoped for, as injuries and trades have decimated their roster. They’ve lost seven games in a row since starting the season 2-0, but are coming out of their bye week. On the other hand, the Steelers won four games in a row prior to last week’s 38-18 loss at Cincinnati. They still sit at 6-3 on the season, though, and are in the playoff picture in their conference – that’s more than the Eagles can say. The Eagles have won the last two meetings, and the Steelers haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965 (a stretch of 11 matchups), but that could change this week. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 11 matchup with a final score prediction. I don't care that the Eagles are coming off their BYE; this is one of the worst teams in the NFL, and the fact that they had expectations heading into this season leads me to believe the locker room isn't exactly experiencing any good vibes either. Quite honestly, I’m surprised this spread isn’t bigger, as I expect the Steelers to cruise to victory in Philadelphia. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football 49ers rout Vikings Tarik Skubal to Mets Week 11 winners and losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners and losers Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. away.blurb: Most of those questions are positive ones for the Steelers - like will wide receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. both return against the Eagles or just one? Will they activate rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker from the IR? But as the positive news mounts, the Steelers are never too far from a setback. With the team's latest injury report ahead of their Week 11 matchup, another player is now the biggest concern. Outside linebacker Nick Herbig did not participate in two previous practices due to a rib and hip injury, and after being designated as not participating in a third straight team session, he has been listed as questionable against the Eagles. Additionally, the Steelers listed Dunker, Pittman, Wilson, inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and safety DeShon Elliott as questionable. Queen is dealing with a fractured thumb he sustained in Week 10, but is expected to play, while Elliott missed Week 10 due to a knee injury he suffered pregame. home.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted!
