picks.blurb: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football 49ers rout Vikings Tarik Skubal to Mets Week 11 winners and losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners and losers Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Calais Campbell #93 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he leads a huddle against the Los Angeles Chargers prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:22 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest. At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21

away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . picks.blurb: Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football 49ers rout Vikings Tarik Skubal to Mets Week 11 winners and losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners and losers Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 (James Lang-Imagn Images) Aiden Checketts · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers finally got in the win column as they picked up their first win of the season, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on the road on Monday Night Football. After winning their first game of the 2026 season, it is going to be interesting to see how LA approaches the rest of the season , and whether they are competitive or end up with a top draft pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, the focus now moves to their home matchup this week against the New York Jets in a game that could have a lot to do with how the draft order pans out. On that note, ESPN put out a Week 11 preview done by NFL Nation as well as fantasy football writer Eric Moody, analytics writer Seth Walder, and sports betting analyst Pamela Maldonado, who picked each game, and when it came to the Chargers and Jets matchup, LA was the unanimous pick. Now, in terms of the picks, Maldonado had the Chargers winning 24-20, Moody had a 23-17 victory for LA, and Walder picked Los Angeles to 23-20. All that to say, it is very clear that this ESPN panel does like the Chargers this week, and despite the fact the season has been rough for LA thus far, sometimes after picking up a win, a team can get into a rhythm and start stacking wins. One thing to note on the Chargers side, is the fact that they did a great job on the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball on Monday night against the Ravens. Starting with the defense, LA held running back Derrick Henry to 10 yards rushing on 10 carries and the Ravens 15 attempts for 16 yards as a team. That is a great performance for LA and because of that, it forced quarterback Jacoby Brissett to put the the game on his shoulders and the Chargers were able to do just enough to get the win through picking him off once and recovering a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers. Now on the offensive side, the Chargers ran the ball very well with running back Omarion Hampton tallying 22 carries for 105 yards and one score in addition to quarterback Justin Herbert adding seven carries for 51 yards and a touchdown. As a team, LA ran the ball 34 times for 160 yards while averaging 4.7 yards per carry. All that to say, the formula for the Chargers in Week 10 was dominating on both sides of the line of scrimmage which worked out and enabled them to pick up a win which was huge for their confidence, but also shows that they do not need to lean on Herbert. So, as the Chargers prepare to take on the Jets in Week 11, it will be interesting to see if LA can pick up another win, but also what the formula might be, because if Los Angeles once again dominates up front, that could be something that the Chargers can lean on for the rest of the year.

The New York Jets could turn to rookie Cade Klubnik for his first NFL start Sunday, with Geno Smith’s ankle injury leaving coach Aaron Glenn without a firm answer at quarterback. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Glenn said. The decision concerns Smith’s health, not an announced benching. Glenn said Monday that Smith would retain the job if healthy, The Associated Press reported . Tests did not reveal a serious ankle injury, but New York still needs to determine whether he can play. The Jets are 2-8 after five consecutive losses. They have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, and a change at quarterback would put a fourth-round pick from Clemson in charge of an offense struggling to finish drives. Klubnik made his professional debut against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception. He also ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn praised the rookie’s mobility Wednesday and said he would continue getting practice opportunities against the first- and second-team defenses. Klubnik had little time to settle in, but his first possession produced a 10-play, 61-yard drive and a field goal. Two scrambles moved the chains on that series, the team reported Monday . He played 37 snaps in relief of Smith. Running back Breece Hall came away encouraged by how Klubnik handled the huddle. Hall said the rookie showed more than he expected while stepping into a game without the preparation afforded a starter. “Just seeing how he came in, that was a huge growth step for him,” Hall said. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, Latest Updates as Chargers QB Enters Concussion Protocol After Loss to Jets
away.blurb: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert entered the NFL's concussion protocol after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the New York Jets. Herbert went 15-of-21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. He added 32 yards and a score on eight carries. The Chargers fell to 1-9 with the loss. Herbert has played all six of his NFL seasons with the Bolts, who selected the ex-Oregon star with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft. His accolades includes the 2020 Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year award, a 2021 Pro Bowl nod and two ninth-place finishes in the NFL MVP race in 2022 and 2024. The Chargers largely struggled over Herbert's first four years save for a lone playoff appearance in 2022, although that wasn't the fault of the quarterback. Jim Harbaugh then arrived in town in 2024, and this team was much-improved in 2024 and 2025, going 11-6 with playoff appearances each season. However, the Chargers have endured a disastrous 2026 season, winning just once through 11 weeks. They are 0-5 at home after Sunday. Trey Lance is QB2 behind Herbert on the depth chart.

away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 7:13 PM . Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (concussion) and cornerback Riley Moss (concussion) were among Denver's players who were not assigned game statuses on the Broncos' final practice report of the week, which indicates they will be available to play. Jones, who exited Denver's Week 8 win over Kansas City with his injury, was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11. Tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) was a full participant in all three practices as he returned to practice this week, but he was ruled out for Sunday's game. Jones, who was listed as questionable after he was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11, was among the team's inactive players. Hufanga appears set to play for the first time since suffering his injury in Week 5 against the Chargers. picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Jaguars, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants don't need to be told how good the Jaguars are; they have seen it on tape this week. Similarly, the Giants don't need to be told they're good, too. They do, after all, lead the NFC East, despite criticisms that the division is weak sauce. They are the only team in the division with a positive point differential (+7). They are also pretty angry about having blown a chance against the Washington Commanders last week, a loss that gives the third-place Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker if the two teams somehow end up with the same win-loss record at the end of the season. All of these factors have some critics snickering about the Giants' current standing. After all, someone has to be in first place, regardless of the division, right? And it's not that the Giants care what those outside of 1925 Giants Drive think about their team. Still, they can certainly make a statement with a convincing upset win over the Jaguars, who, surprisingly, FanDuel Sportsbook lists as only a 5.5-point favorite over Big Blue. Will the Giants come through and get their first home win since a 36-24 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 4, 2026? Let's dive in. Why the Giants Will Win The easiest way for the Giants to win this game is to keep the Jaguars offense off the field. And it just so happens that the Giants are currently second in the league in average time of possession (32:26), behind the league-leading Chicago Bears (34:31). That's not bad considering the Giants' rushing game ranks 18th in the league (112.6 yards per game). Big Blue averages 5.7 plays per drive, tying it for seventh in the league (Jacksonville averages 5.8 plays per drive, for those wondering). Nov 15, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) yells to the bench against the Tennessee Titans during the first half at Nissan Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In a nutshell, winning the time-of-possession battle will be key for the Giants if they want to secure a win. The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. In a nutshell, winning the time-of-possession battle will be key for the Giants if they want to secure a win. The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. Defensively, the Giants have been strong against the deep ball, which just so happens to be Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence's superpower. Lawrence has a 51.6 percent completion rate on passes of 20-plus air yards this season, fifth in the league. The Giants have a 38.4 percent blitz rate this season, fourth in the league, and have blitzed on 50 percent or more of their plays since Week 4, a 20 percent increase from the first three weeks. In terms of coverage, the Giants lead the league with a 17.2 percent completion rate allowed on deep balls of 20-plus air yards. They are also the only team not to allow a touchdown on a deep pass attempt, and they have four interceptions on those passes, tied for second in the league. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Jaguars Two potential reasons could doom the Giants' chances of scoring their first home win in over a month. The first is turnovers. The opportunistic Jaguars lead the league with a +9 turnover differential, having 16 takeaways to only seven giveaways. The Jaguars' takeaways include 12 interceptions ( fourth in the league ). The Giants currently have a -2 turnover differential, 21st in the league. They have three giveaways in their last three games (one interception and two lost fumbles). Fumbling has been an issue for the Giants, who have had six fumbles in their last two games. That's not good against an opportunistic Jacksonville team that is averaging 2.3 takeaways over its last three games. Give the Jaguars a short field to work with, and that's asking for trouble. The other thing to watch is the Jaguars' first-half scoring. The Jaguars lead the league in first-half scoring, averaging 15.89 points within the first 30 minutes of regulation. The Giants, meanwhile, have averaged 9.44 points per game in the first half. Needless to say, the Giants do not want to get into a situation where, late in the third or early in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars are so far ahead that Lawrence and other key starters get the rest of the afternoon off. The Jaguars have answered almost every challenge that has come their way during the Liam Coen era, and this is another chance to meet the high expectations and standards that the Jaguars have created. "But any given Sunday—the NFL is the NFL. I was with the Rams in ‘22 when you lost to the 0-13 Jets. It is any given Sunday, anything can happen. And I do think our group believes that. Let's go put together four quarters of our best because we have yet to do it yet.” So, how do the national predictions see this one playing out as the Jaguars make a push in the AFC? For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football 49ers rout Vikings Tarik Skubal to Mets Week 11 winners and losers Tom Jackson dies College football winners and losers NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrated his team's 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars by doing something he said he said he wouldn't do again: a backflip. away.headline: Colton McKivitz Suffers Gruesome Leg Injury, Latest on 49ers OL After Being Carted Off vs. Vikings
away.blurb: San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome leg injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the season after he was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. "It's brutal," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner . "He's somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He's the standard, and we're going to really miss him. We all love him. We're praying for him. It's one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we're going to play for him from here on out." Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sent his well wishes upon seeing the injury. The injury comes amid what has been a career year for McKivitz, who has the second-best PFF run block grade among tackles and the seventh-best overall grade among tackles. McKivitz has been a starter on the Niners' offensive line and has played all 17 games of the season since 2023. He has yet to miss a game this season, though that streak will surely come to an end. While McKivitz has established himself as a starter, the 30-year-old has had a long road to get to that point. He was a fifth-round draft pick in 2020 and started a handful of games as a rookie, but was waived ahead of the 2021 season, and had to work his way back onto the active roster via the practice squad. Eventually, he earned the job as a full-time starter ahead of the 2023 campaign, and he's stayed there ever since. He signed a three-year, $45 million deal this offseason despite perhaps being able to earn more elsewhere. "I want to be on that 10-year wall," McKivitz said after signing that deal. "I don't want to leave here. Obviously being cut, I've got some scars there. But, there was a reason why I was drafted here, why I was cut here, and why I still play here. Now I've had three good seasons of starting and I'm going into the fourth." Clearly, McKivitz is well loved and well respected by his teammates, which explains the emotional reaction from them after the injury.

away.headline: NFL-49ers rout Vikings as NFL makes electrifying return to Mexico
away.blurb: MEXICO CITY, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The San Francisco 49ers overwhelmed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday at the Azteca Stadium, as the National Football League made a thrilling return to Mexico City after a four-year absence with its first international Sunday Night Football game. The halftime show featured Mexican rock trio The Warning, as the break was extended by six minutes to accommodate the teams' return from locker rooms located outside the stadium. By Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina More than 85,000 fans, most of them backing the 49ers, filled the stadium, underlining the popularity of the sport in Mexico, which is the NFL's largest market outside the US. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell had described the occasion as a "mini-Super Bowl", underlining the importance of a country that has hosted five previous regular-season games since the league first played in Mexico in 2005. San Francisco quickly gave its supporters something to cheer when tight end George Kittle opened the scoring on the 49ers' first possession. Kittle, one of the most popular players among Mexican fans, added another touchdown in the second quarter, his fourth in the Mexican capital. Minnesota responded with an 11-yard touchdown run by Aaron Jones but struggled to cope with San Francisco's offense and the deafening noise inside the stadium. The 49ers extended their lead through a touchdown pass from quarterback Brock Purdy to Mike Evans before safety Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned the ball 18 yards for a touchdown to make it 28-10 at halftime. The 49ers' right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field on a stretcher after suffering a lower-leg injury in the second quarter, prompting an emotional reaction from teammates. Purdy cemented his status as an MVP contender with a dominant performance against a Minnesota defense that had entered the game allowing an NFL-best 14 points per contest. He threw three touchdown passes in the first half alone. San Francisco maintained control after the interval, with cornerback Deommodore Lenoir forcing a fumble from Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson in the third quarter. Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the final quarter to stretch the lead as visibly fatigued players used oxygen masks on the sidelines to cope with the effects of playing at an altitude of more than 2,200 meters (7,217 ft) above sea level. Some Minnesota supporters began leaving the stands as their team struggled to mount a comeback. San Francisco had made special preparations for the altitude, spending the week training at the US Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota remained at home and used a specially constructed altitude-training room at its facility. The matchup was the final stop on the NFL's record nine-game international schedule this season. (Reporting by Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina in Mexico City)

away.headline: Vikings-49ers Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. Kittle, one of the most popular players among Mexican fans, added another touchdown in the second quarter, his fourth in the Mexican capital. Minnesota responded with an 11-yard touchdown run by Aaron Jones but struggled to cope with San Francisco's offense and the deafening noise inside the stadium. The 49ers extended their lead through a touchdown pass from quarterback Brock Purdy to Mike Evans before safety Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned the ball 18 yards for a touchdown to make it 28-10 at halftime. The 49ers' right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field on a stretcher after suffering a lower-leg injury in the second quarter, prompting an emotional reaction from teammates. Purdy cemented his status as an MVP contender with a dominant performance against a Minnesota defense that had entered the game allowing an NFL-best 14 points per contest. He threw three touchdown passes in the first half alone. San Francisco maintained control after the interval, with cornerback Deommodore Lenoir forcing a fumble from Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson in the third quarter. Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the final quarter to stretch the lead as visibly fatigued players used oxygen masks on the sidelines to cope with the effects of playing at an altitude of more than 2,200 meters (7,217 ft) above sea level. Some Minnesota supporters began leaving the stands as their team struggled to mount a comeback. San Francisco had made special preparations for the altitude, spending the week training at the US Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota remained at home and used a specially constructed altitude-training room at its facility. The matchup was the final stop on the NFL's record nine-game international schedule this season. (Reporting by Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina in Mexico City)

home.headline: Vikings-49ers Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Monday night contest in DC Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals . Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival New York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks. Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night. Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Commanders vs. Bengals live Date: Monday, Nov. 23 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Northwest Stadium (Landover, Maryland) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -6, O/U 54.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bengals have the ball Joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL . Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease. Ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him. The Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment. Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample , though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two. Washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league. However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins. When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams . Without Terry McLaurin , Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs , rookie Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo. Diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position. The Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year. The Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler , each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football. With big Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins , Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground. The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. away.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals LB Oren Burks (groin) and OG Dalton Risner did not practice this week and are listed as out on Saturday, Nov. 21's final injury report for Week 11's game against the Washington Commanders . Burks was also placed on the reserve/injured list. WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb) and CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) practiced in full and are listed as doubtful, with both needing to be activated off the reserve/injured list to play in Week 11. CB Daxton Hill (illness) did not practice this week and is listed as questionable. OG Dylan Fairchild (oblique) practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday, but practiced in full on Saturday and is listed as questionable. S Kyle Dugger (quad) practiced in a limited fashion on Thursday, but practiced in full on Friday and Saturday and is listed as questionable. OG Brian Parker II (knee) practiced in full this week and is listed as questionable, needing to be activated off the reserve/injured list to play in Week 11. LB Swayze Bozeman (forearm) practiced in full this week and is listed as questionable. DT B.J. Hill (NIR-Rest) did not practice on Friday and Saturday and has no injury designation. DT Dexter Lawrence (NIR-Rest) did not practice on Saturday and has no injury designation. DE Jonathan Allen (NIR-Rest) did not practice on Thursday and Friday, but practiced in a limited capacity on Saturday and has no injury designation. QB Joe Burrow (illness), WR Tee Higgins (knee), OT Myles Hinton (illness), and S P.J. Jules (ankle) all practiced in full this week and have no injury designation. away.blurb: Starting right guard Dalton Risner exited Sunday’s game in the middle of the second quarter. He was questionable to play at all with an illness, but has also been dealing with a knee injury for most of the season. Dylan Fairchild’s not out of the woods yet, either Fairchild was able to play the whole game until some of the starters were taken out during garbage time in the fourth quarter. He was day-to-day upon coming back from Madrid, but ended up as a full participant to end the week of practice. This is where rookie Brian Parker II would come in handy. Parker was designated to return off of Injured Reserve late last week , indicating he is very close to being able to play after suffering a knee injury to end the preseason. He played LG quite admirably in the preseason. He may just be their best option at the position in Fairchild can’t go. Cincinnati has been blessed with tremendous continuity along it’s o-line. That continuity was challenged on Sunday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it will be a story to watch over the next seven days as well. The Cincinnati Bengals offensive line has been able to handle all kinds of competition this season. They could be facing their biggest opponent this week, and it’s not the Washington Commanders. away.headline: Commanders injury updates: Four questionable vs Bengals on Monday
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. away.headline: Bengals' Joe Burrow updates his status before Week 11
away.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow looks and sounds like a man on the mend after an illness. One day removed from missing his weekly press conference , Burrow held it on Friday and updated reporters on his status. In short, Burrow said things have been “not bad” on the illness front and that he is “getting better,” to keep it simple. From the sounds of it, there’s something small sweeping through the locker room, but Burrow said he was happy with the energy levels on Friday for the second practice of the week. Given Burrow’s participation in practice and his holding the presser on Friday, things sound on track for the Bengals . But it probably doesn't hurt that they’re the Monday night game this week when they play the Washington Commanders, either. This article originally appeared on Bengals Wire: Bengals' Joe Burrow updates his status before Week 11

home.headline: Washington Commanders 2026 Week 10 Stats Roundup – Offense
home.blurb: Franchise QB Jayden Daniels , is currently the 14 th ranked QB by total QBR, just a little above league average. That is not bad for a QB working with up and down pass protection and a rag-tag band of backups and injury replacements for a supporting cast. One area where he really stands out is protecting the football. Prior to throwing two picks against the Giants, last week, he was the leader in TWP%. Even after the two picks, he is near the top of the league in ball security. Yards Before Contact per Rushing Attempt (YBC/Att) reflects a combination of two factors: RB elusiveness and run blocking. As such, it is more an indicator of the health of the rushing offense, overall, than an individual player stat. That said, when one RB on team stands out from the others, it can be taken as an indicator of RB performance. Before his season ending injury, Jeremy McNichols averaged just 3.4 Y/A on 10 carries. He is often used in short yardage situations, where his 70.0% success rate might be a better indicator of his value to the team, albeit in a limited sample. He averaged 2.2 YBC/Att, just like Bill and Rachaad. I have settled on PFF Run Blocking Grades to quantify run blocking performance because they're readily available, and I haven't found anything with more analytic rigor behind it. PFF's grades are derived by analysts scoring every play of every game on a five point scale based on a subjective assessment of a player's contribution to the success of the play. PFF does not disclose the grading criteria used for each of their player grades, but we can at least infer that they use standardized protocols, because they do disclose that they employ a quality control process in which analysts' grades are checked and corrected by more senior analysts before publication to ensure that all analysts are grading plays the same way. Quality control is critical when working with subjective assessments as a check on observer bias. Chris Paul is the next ranked pass protector after Cosmi, ranking 4 th out of 67 guards. But there is a bit of a gap between the players' pressure rates. The not so great news is that Paul has consistently ranked among the worst guards at run blocking from week to week. Only Tennessee's Atonio Mafi was graded below him. home.headline: Injury Report: Washington Commanders vs. Cincinnati Bengals
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders will enter week 11 with four players ruled questionable. The final injury report released on Saturday listed running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, cornerback Amik Robertson, offensive lineman Lucas Patrick and running back Rachaad White as questionable, hours after head coach Dan Quinn expressed optimism surrounding the status of several players. That included Croskey-Merritt, who Quinn pointed to as trending in the right direction to make his first long-awaited return. Croskey-Merritt was sidelined in the week six loss against the San Francisco 49ers with a groin injury, but saw his 21 day practice window officially opened to begin the practice week. Quinn also confirmed that Patrick is set to return as the team's starting center prior to the injury report being released. Patrick was sidelined in the week ten win after remaining in concussion protocol, an injury suffered the week prior. Washington turned to Nick Allegretti as the starter in week ten after rookie Lucas Patrick replaced him in the second half against the Los Angeles Rams. The status of Croskey-Merritt looms large with uncertainty about White after being a limited participant on Friday before not suiting up for Saturday's practice. White was the one who primarily stepped up in the running back room to replace Croskey-Merritt's production, doing so efficiently after tallying one rushing touchdown and averaging nearly 4.5 yards per carry over his last three games. Head coach Dan Quinn ponted to the chance to sit White during practice in an effort to reduce the soreness as he battles through a heel injury. Cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the final play of Friday's practice, leading him to become a limited participant during Saturday's practice. After pointing to the 48 hours ahead as a chance to evaluate his status ahead of kickoff, Quinn also pointed to Rasul Douglas and a combination of Mike Sainristil and Fabian Moreau inside to mitigate his absence. Yet the Bengals will also work through a notable injury in the trenches with starting right guard Dalton Risner ruled out due to a knee injury. He joins linebacker Oren Burks as inactives for Cincinnati. Meanwhile, safety Kyle Duggar, guard Dylan Fairchild, cornerback Daxton Hill and guard Brian Parker II have all been ruled questionable ahead of Monday night.
